purpose: Whether the intent-fidelity gate separates a protocol that says the approved science in other words from one that says other science, and whether it refuses to decide what nobody approved.
note: Frozen. Do not edit this file. benchmark_v1 is unchanged and still carries the pipeline cases; v2 adds the fidelity suite and inherits v1's cases by reference rather than copying them.
why_v2: v1 measured whether the pipeline builds the approved study. It could not measure the gate's discrimination, because it contained one question and no faithful rewordings: a checker that blocked everything would have scored the same. v2 adds the classes a gate has to tell apart, including the two it is most likely to get wrong -- a faithful paraphrase read as drift, and an unapproved choice read as approved.
precedence_under_test: 2 Research Question as framing and context

labels.FAITHFUL: the protocol expresses the approved science; expected PASS
labels.DRIFTED: the protocol expresses different science; expected FAIL
labels.AMBIGUOUS: a scientifically necessary choice no approved source makes; expected NEEDS_HUMAN, never PASS and never FAIL

scoring.detection_recall: DRIFTED cases returned FAIL / all DRIFTED cases
scoring.precision: DRIFTED cases returned FAIL / all cases returned FAIL
scoring.false_block_rate: FAITHFUL cases not returned PASS / all FAITHFUL cases
scoring.ambiguity_escalation_rate: AMBIGUOUS cases returned NEEDS_HUMAN / all AMBIGUOUS cases
scoring.note: Expected codes are pre-registered. A case answered with the right verdict but a different code is counted as detected and recorded as a code mismatch; it is not silently reclassified.

protocol_construction: Each case builds the baseline controlled_llm protocol from the approved hypothesis (or the question, when there is no hypothesis) and then applies protocol_overrides. An empty override set means the protocol is the baseline.
